question: repair the retrieval step or remove it by judging the whole artifact
measured_failure: 7 of 18 pipeline negatives overturn under two-judge full-artifact review, split 4 of 9 on no-span items and 3 of 9 on poor-span items

measured_cost.method: three items judged both ways by the same judge in structured output mode, tokens and cost read from the usage stream

decision: judge the whole artifact as the primary path and retain the span-based verdict on a twenty percent subsample as a drift check, rather than repairing cue retrieval
why_not_repair: the failure is not a tuning problem in one direction. Three of the four no-span misses were the same element stated in wording the cues do not match, and poor spans fail at a similar rate, so widening cues would trade one silent miss for a different one without a recall measurement to bound it.
why_keep_a_subsample: the full-artifact view is the reference that overturned the pipeline, and it has never itself been validated. Keeping the cheaper verdict on a subsample makes disagreement between the two visible instead of assuming the wider view is right.
honest_limit: no accuracy measurement exists for full-artifact judging either. This decision removes a measured failure mode and accepts an unmeasured one, which is a defensible trade only because the removed one is quantified and directional.
does_not_affect_Q0007: the completion arm needs no judging at all, since completion is decided by the admission path, so this cost belongs to the quality arm and does not change the pending spend question
